content:
alex: customer (acct: acme-inc) opened a high-priority ticket — multiple 5xx/timeouts on hosted inference around eastus3 AZ-B since ~10:12 UTC. They see auth retries and token refresh failures. linking their support log: https://acme.support/CI-2345 :exclamation:

camille: thanks. any internal alerts?

oncall-bot: ALERT: hosted-inference.eastus3.az-b 5xx-rate spike (5m avg) -> 14.7% 

sanjay: seeing increased 502/504s from gateway metrics for eastus3 az-b. also elevated connection resets on upstream pool. not global, AZ-B only.

alex: paste from customer repro curl (redacted):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
> HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
> Connection reset by peer
```

alex: customer also sent a tcpdump snippet showing retransmits and dup acks around the token exchange window.

luis: can you share a quick traceroute from our edge to their region? also drop a sample of `ss -tanp` on the gateway host if available.

alex: attaching internal trace from relay -> az-b edge (shortened):
```
10.2.14.5 -> 198.51.100.23 (provider hop) * *
198.51.100.23 -> 203.0.113.8  120 ms  121 ms  118 ms  (ECMP path flip)
203.0.113.8 -> 198.51.100.23  300 ms  *  280 ms  (dup/long RTT)
```

camille: that looks like path oscillation at the transit/provider hop. I see ECMP flips and asymmetric return latency. likely packet loss causing TLS handshake timeouts during auth refresh.

sanjay: confirmed from netmetrics: az-b interface eth1 shows microburst packet loss and retransmit counts spiking at 10:11:30 - 10:18:00 UTC across multiple hosts. correlates exactly with customer window.

luis: mitigation idea — enable sticky routing to steer traffic away from the flapping ECMP hash for a few minutes and bump health checks to avoid routing to degraded pool. can we do a graceful drain of az-b workers?

camille: starting coarse mitigation: marking provider-path-unhealthy for az-b from control-plane routing; initiating failover to az-a for new sessions. doing small drain on az-b API frontends now.

alex: customer asked about billing impact and wants repro steps for their internal team. they also flagged that some of their ingestion jobs retried aggressively and incurred extra token usage.

sanjay: please capture a sample of the error-rate / token-usage delta during the spike for billing team. I'll annotate it for customer.

oncall-bot: NOTE: automated failover to az-a completed at 10:20:45 UTC. 5xx rate dropped to 1.8% in 5m window.

camille: provider acknowledged a micro-outage on one POP interconnect, reporting BGP flap + ECMP recalculation. they've opened a ticket with their NOC and are doing route dampening.

alex: shared repro steps with customer: short script they used to reproduce (sanitized):
```
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}' || echo "err $i"; done
```
advised: run from different AZ / add jitter between calls.

alex: customer wants credits for the excess token charges and an RCA. they escalated to their procurement SLA.

luis: I'll export token-usage delta and attach per-minute spike chart for billing. add tags: `provider-egress`, `az-b`, `auth-retries`.

sanjay: root cause (preliminary): intermittent packet loss and ECMP path flapping at a transit provider POP impacting eastus3 AZ-B. effect: TLS handshake timeouts and increased auth token retries causing gateway 5xx during token exchange windows.

camille: status: mitigated via failover. provider ticket open (ref: TP-6789). next steps: confirm provider RFO, verify no residual cache/inflight sessions in az-b, run two-hour postmortem window, and prepare customer RCA + billing adjustment note.

alex: I'll draft the customer update and post here. cc: @support-team.

customer-jira-bot: Ticket ACME-2345 updated: "Redwood mitigation applied; investigating provider POP"

luis: action items assigned: billing export (luis), provider follow-up (camille), rca draft (alex), infra tweak to health-check thresholds (sanjay).

alex: closing loop with customer: we applied automatic failover and reduced 5xxs; we will issue a billing credit once billing confirms token-delta. they acknowledged and will keep monitor on their side. :white_check_mark:

camille: long-term mitigation idea: implement short-term session-layer retry/backoff for auth refresh and increase jitter on client-side SDK to reduce retry storms during transient network issues.

sanjay: agreed — also adding a playbook entry for "region provider pop flap" with runbook steps for graceful drain and traffic steering.

alex: thanks all — keeping thread open until provider RFO published.
